head: f5395d6dc3375294877f9b3b03592fdb60a60d9d
classification_reasons: Blast radius: the change is to the authorization of the runbook Go, the one gate before a running-system action runs with the runbook secrets. It touches the risk-list item 'auth'.

Spec tightness: tight. Every flagged concern is decided (auth by decision 35, the fixture edit by panel decision 1, the label that stays). The acceptance can be measured: two named tests with stated assertions, eight existing Go tests unchanged in body, and the three targets.

Test coverage: the Go path is covered, but the fix needs a declared test-infrastructure edit (a GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER line in the rollback_incident fixture) in a fix-type change, so it is not covered by the existing tests as they stand.
attempted: Intent: the intent wants cli.py:1183 to stop accepting any person's sdlc:go, with a reproducing test written first. The spec puts is_owner_actor after the bot and automation branch of _human_label_actor, against the approved copy. That is the intent's suggested patch with a top-level import and a reason text that follows R5. It solves the stated problem.

Spec and plan: R1 to R10 each map to a plan step or a proof line. Two files are listed, in the order test then fix. The panel decision's three conditions are all in plan.md: the fixture line goes in the reproducing-test commit before lock-tests; the step-1 log runs the module with the fixture line alone; the Risks line names owner_login as the only direct reader and lists the seven indirect callers. The spec's Flagged concerns record the decision.
Claim: _human_label_actor(repo, number, label, config) is at cli.py:1179-1188 and its last refusal is the bot/automation branch. Checked; true.

Claim: cmd_go passes `approved` (_approved_config, fail closed) to _human_label_actor before _judge, and a (None, why) emits performed:false and exits 0 without touching labels, status or the runbook. Checked at cli.py:1201-1218; true.

Claim: is_owner_actor/owner_login read sdlc.yaml:owner, then GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER, then GITHUB_REPOSITORY or repo; they ignore case and fail closed on an empty actor, a [bot], the automation identity and an unknown owner. Checked at unpark.py:78-115; true. R2 omits the GITHUB_REPOSITORY step, which is harmless.

Claim: there is no import cycle. Checked: unpark imports state.conventions and state.status at the top, and gate.policy and pr.github lazily, nothing from detect. detect/cli.py already uses the sys.path plus '# noqa: E402' pattern at lines 50-61, so the plan's E402 import matches.

Claim (the corrected Risks line): GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER reaches no is_owner_actor caller under the rollback_incident fixture. Checked further: cmd_go's _gate_and_pr runs gate/cli.py and pr/cli.py as subprocesses that inherit os.environ (_cli at cli.py:134 passes no env), so the variable does reach them. However, gate/checks.py imports only is_automation_actor and runner-reset helpers from unpark, and pr/cli.py reaches review_request (owner_login) only after a GitHub repo is resolved. The tests' bare local origin returns 'no GitHub remote' at pr/cli.py:157 first. The claim holds in effect, and the step-1 log is the stated check.

Claim: five existing Go tests use actor 'the-owner' on REPO 'o/r' with no owner named and would fail without the fixture line. Checked (tests/test_detect_cli.py:789, 843, 1296, 1690 head case, 2040 go case); true. With the fixture, the main case of the automation-identity test still refuses at the bot/automation branch first, with the same reason, which meets R6's order. The rewritten-origin and unreadable-copy tests refuse before the actor check.

Claim: tests/conftest.py removes every GITHUB_* variable and tells a test to set the one it needs through monkeypatch. Checked at lines 14-21 and 78-84; true. The fixture's monkeypatch is the same function-scoped instance the tests use, so the tests that also setenv/delenv other variables are unaffected.

Claim: the new main case orders the-owner's Go (refused, because owner: colleague on origin/main overrides GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER) before the colleague's Go (which runs). Checked: the order is needed because after a run the record says 'ran', and a later Go is refused with 'did not ask for Go'. On today's code the-owner's half runs the runbook, so the test fails before the fix as step 1 says. The head case fails today because the colleague passes the bot check. Neither can pass with the bug present.

Claim: the template's sdlc.yaml has no active owner: key, so appending 'owner: colleague' creates no duplicate key and the fixture project's main names no owner. The previous round checked this and it is unchanged here. load_sdlc_config has no owner-specific rule that would reject the key.

Decisions: 14 (Go is the owner's per-incident act) and 34 point 3 (one function, fail closed, the default branch's owner; a workflow if: is only a coarse check). The design matches both and leaves sdlc-runbook.yml unchanged.

Proof: design phase, so there is no toolchain log to compare. The plan names the two new tests with their assertions, says each fails on 80d7de5 before the fix, and requires the step-1 log with the fixture line alone.

Tests: no pre-existing test body or assertion changes. The fixture line is declared in the spec, the plan and the panel decision, and sits before the lock. It does not weaken what any test proves: the existing tests still assert that the runbook runs for the now explicit owner, and the new tests prove a non-owner is refused.

Blast radius: one caller (cmd_go). No data shape, schema, migration, workflow or guardrail file changes. The diff stays inside the change folder. The by-hand route still resolves the owner from --repo. The intended narrowing affects live projects where a collaborator gave the Go and organization repositories with no owner: key; the brief records both.

Policies: security-baseline rule 1 (the server-side check in the step that holds the secrets, against the default branch's copy), rule 3 (no credential) and rule 6 (no new dependency). Coding-standards rule 4 (test first, nothing weakened). ux-and-brand rule 4 (the reason names the label, the actor and the owner requirement, and says the label stays). All applied.
Skip markers: not checked at design (the ratchets check runs at build and test).
